explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/405: 'Erdős and Graham ask this allowing the case p = 2, but this is presumably an oversight, since clearly there are infinitely many solutions to this equation when p = 2.' The Lean statement: the set of triples (a, k, p) with p prime (2 allowed) and (p−1)! + a^{p−1} = p^k is infinite, proved in the file via the family (2^k − 1, k, 2), i.e. 1 + (2^k − 1) = 2^k. Faithful.
